question_a_classification.answer: The model can distinguish positive from negative file rows globally.
question_a_classification.evidence: Dataset contains 1055 positive and 53334 negative file rows. Global classification metrics measure this ability.

question_b_ranking.answer: The dataset provides NO supervision for ranking files within a commit.
question_b_ranking.evidence: Zero mixed commits exist. All positive commits label every file as positive, providing no signal to distinguish risky from safe files within a commit.

reasoning: All 210 positive commits are all-positive (100.0%). 210/210 positive commits use commit-level attribution (explicit SHA reference or revert). 0 commits use file-level attribution (line overlap). The labeling methodology cannot distinguish implicated files from unrelated files within the same commit. File-level risk ranking requires mixed commits where some files are positive and others are negative.
root_cause: The labeling methodology uses commit-level attribution for all positive labels in the dataset. No file-level attribution (line overlap) was successfully applied.
